# Fix LLM Status Panel Environment Variable Warnings and Display Source

## Why
PR #4782 addressed issue #4679, but verification reported **CONCERNS**. The status panel still (1) fails to warn when only *some* required env vars are missing, (2) can display provider/model values that lag behind the user's current sidebar selection, and (3) treats unknown providers as if they require no configuration. This follow-up closes those gaps with clear UI behavior and regression tests, including protections against leaking secret env var values into the UI.

## Source
- Original PR: #4782
- Parent issue: #4679

## Tasks

### Missing Environment Variable Warning Logic
- [ ] Implement the missing environment variable computation logic that creates `required_vars` from `_llm_required_env_vars(selected_provider)` and filters to `missing_vars` using `_llm_env_var_present(v)` checks
- [ ] Update the warning display logic to call `st.warning()` exactly once when `missing_vars` is non-empty with a formatted message containing all missing variable names

### Status Panel Display Source of Truth
- [ ] Update status panel provider/model sourcing to read `st.session_state.selected_provider` and `st.session_state.selected_model` (with safe defaults) for display values
- [ ] Ensure `_resolve_llm_provider_config()` is used only for backend instantiation, not for status panel display values
- [ ] Update sidebar selection code to write current selection to `st.session_state.selected_provider` and `st.session_state.selected_model` on change

### Unknown Provider Handling
- [ ] Update `_llm_required_env_vars()` to log a warning and return `None` (or raise a controlled exception) when provider is not recognized
- [ ] Update `_render_llm_status_panel()` to render an "Unknown provider" message when `_llm_required_env_vars()` returns sentinel/raises controlled exception

### Unit Tests: Environment Variable Warning Behavior
- [ ] Write a unit test that mocks missing environment variables and asserts `st.warning()` is called exactly once with all missing variable names in the warning text
- [ ] Write a unit test that mocks all required environment variables as present and asserts `st.warning()` is never called
- [ ] Write a unit test that verifies partial environment variable configuration triggers a warning containing only the missing variable names

### Unit Tests: Status Panel Display Source
- [ ] Create a test fixture that sets up `st.session_state.selected_provider` and `st.session_state.selected_model` with known test values
- [ ] Write a unit test that verifies the status panel renders the provider value from `st.session_state.selected_provider` by inspecting Streamlit render call arguments
- [ ] Write a unit test that verifies the status panel renders the model value from `st.session_state.selected_model` by inspecting Streamlit render call arguments
- [ ] Write a unit test that confirms the status panel does not use values from `_resolve_llm_provider_config()` for display purposes

### Unit Tests: Secret Value Leakage Prevention
- [ ] Create a test fixture that seeds fake API key values into `os.environ` for secret leakage detection tests
- [ ] Write a unit test that captures all Streamlit UI calls and asserts seeded secret values never appear in any positional arguments
- [ ] Write a unit test that captures all Streamlit UI calls and asserts seeded secret values never appear in any keyword arguments like `value`, `placeholder`, `help`, or `label`
- [ ] Write a unit test that verifies environment variable NAMES are allowed to appear in UI calls while VALUES are prohibited

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `_render_llm_status_panel()` computes missing env vars using: `required_vars = _llm_required_env_vars(selected_provider)` and `missing_vars = [v for v in required_vars if not _llm_env_var_present(v)]`, and if `missing_vars` is non-empty it calls `st.warning()` exactly once with a message that contains every missing var name (each name appears as a substring in the warning text)
- [ ] When all required env vars are present for the selected provider, `_render_llm_status_panel()` does not call `st.warning()`
- [ ] If one or more required env vars are missing, the warning text lists ALL missing names in a single warning (no multiple warnings)
- [ ] The status panel displays provider and model from `st.session_state.selected_provider` and `st.session_state.selected_model` (or defined safe defaults when absent) and does not use `_resolve_llm_provider_config()` output values for the displayed provider/model text
- [ ] The sidebar selection code writes the current selection to `st.session_state.selected_provider` and `st.session_state.selected_model` on change, and these keys are the sole source-of-truth for what the status panel displays
- [ ] `_llm_required_env_vars(provider)` does not return an empty list for an unrecognized provider; instead it logs a warning and returns a sentinel (`None`) OR raises a controlled exception that is handled by the UI
- [ ] When the selected provider is unknown (as determined by `_llm_required_env_vars` returning sentinel/raising controlled exception), `_render_llm_status_panel()` renders an "Unknown provider" message and does not render a "no env vars required" state for that provider
- [ ] No Streamlit UI call made during `_render_llm_status_panel()` includes any environment variable VALUES (e.g., API keys) in any positional args or kwargs such as `value`/`placeholder`/`help`/`label`; only env var NAMES may appear
- [ ] The env-var warning message contains env var NAMES only and does not contain env var VALUES even when those env vars are set in `os.environ`
- [ ] All new unit tests pass and achieve coverage of the modified code paths

## Implementation Notes

**Code Changes:**
- Status panel rendering: Implement missing-var computation, single-warning rendering, unknown-provider UI, and session_state-based display
- Sidebar selection: Ensure explicit assignments to `st.session_state.selected_provider` and `st.session_state.selected_model` on change
- `_llm_required_env_vars()`: Change unknown-provider behavior to log a warning and return sentinel (`None`) or raise controlled exception; ensure UI handles it explicitly

**Test Infrastructure:**
- Add/extend test files to provide Streamlit mock/harness that captures calls (`st.warning`, `st.write`, `st.markdown`, `st.caption`, `st.text_input`, etc.)
- For env var checks, patch helper functions (`_llm_required_env_vars`, `_llm_env_var_present`) to make tests deterministic
- For secret leakage tests, seed `os.environ` with fake values and collect all captured Streamlit calls' args/kwargs, stringifying them to assert seeded secret values are absent
- Align unknown-provider behavior (return `None` vs raise) with repo conventions; ensure tests match the chosen behavior

<details>
<summary>Background (previous attempt context)</summary>

**Failure to avoid: Using the condition `if not any(status.values())` to determine missing environment variables**
- Why it failed: This only triggers when *all* expected environment variables are missing; partial misconfiguration (some missing) incorrectly appears valid
- What to do instead: Iterate over required env vars; if any are missing, compile the full missing list and call `st.warning()` once with all missing names

**Failure to avoid: Relying solely on the resolved provider from `_resolve_llm_provider_config()` for the status panel**
- Why it failed: Can mismatch the user's current sidebar selection due to resolution logic differences/lag
- What to do instead: Display provider/model directly from `st.session_state.selected_provider` / `st.session_state.selected_model` (with safe defaults), using resolution only for backend instantiation

</details>

items.title: opencode-mem/issues #16: [Bug] OpenAI API rejects temperature parameter when using gpt-5-mini/nano (reasoning models)
items.content:
## Environment
- **OS**: macOS (Apple Silicon, arm64)
- **opencode-mem version**: 2.7.4
- **opencode version**: 1.1.50
- **memoryProvider**: `openai-chat`
- **memoryModel**: `gpt-5-mini`

## Bug

When `memoryModel` is set to `gpt-5-mini` (or any GPT-5 family model), all AI-powered features fail with a 400 error because opencode-mem sends `temperature: 0.3` which reasoning models don't support.

### Error (repeated continuously in logs)

```log
[2026-02-06T13:04:25.146Z] OpenAI Chat Completion API error: {"status":400,"error":"{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"message\": \"Unsupported value: 'temperature' does not support 0.3 with this model. Only the default (1) value is supported.\",\n    \"type\": \"invalid_request_error\",\n    \"param\": \"temperature\",\n    \"code\": \"unsupported_value\"\n  }\n}"}
[2026-02-06T13:04:25.146Z] Idle processing error: ...
```

This error fires on every idle processing cycle, spamming the log file indefinitely.

### Impact

All AI-dependent features are broken:
- Idle memory analysis / auto-capture
- User profile generation
- Any other provider-backed operations

Basic memory operations (add/list/forget) still work since they don't use the AI provider. Vector search also works since it uses the local embedding model.

### Root Cause

GPT-5 family models (`gpt-5`, `gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5-nano`) are reasoning models and do not support the `temperature`, `top_p`, `presence_penalty`, or `frequency_penalty` parameters. OpenAI returns a 400 error if any of these are included.

The temperature value appears to be hardcoded in the OpenAI chat completion provider (`dist/services/ai/providers/openai-chat-completion.js`).

### Suggested Fix

Before sending the API request, check if the model is a reasoning model and omit unsupported parameters:

```javascript
const isReasoningModel = model.startsWith("gpt-5") || model.startsWith("o1") || model.startsWith("o3") || model.startsWith("o4");

const requestBody = {
  model,
  messages,
  ...(isReasoningModel ? {} : { temperature: 0.3 }),
  // same for top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty if used
};
```

Alternatively, allow the user to override or disable the temperature in the config file.

### Workaround

Switch `memoryModel` to a non-reasoning model that supports temperature, e.g. `gpt-4.1-mini`:

```jsonc
{
  "memoryModel": "gpt-4.1-mini"
}
```

items.title: opencode-antigravity-auth/issues #400: fix: bypass soft quota check for gemini-cli requests
items.content:
## Problem
The `AccountManager` incorrectly applies the Antigravity soft quota check to `gemini-cli` requests. When an account has exhausted its Antigravity quota (100% usage), `isOverSoftQuotaThreshold` returns `true`. This causes the account selection logic to skip the account, even if `cli_first` is enabled or the CLI pool is explicitly requested.

## Impact
Users cannot utilize the `gemini-cli` pool as a fallback when their Antigravity quota is full.

## Proposed Fix
Modify `src/plugin/accounts.ts` to bypass the soft quota check when the requested `headerStyle` is `gemini-cli`.

### Changes in `src/plugin/accounts.ts`
- Updated `getCurrentOrNextForFamily` (both hybrid and sticky paths) to skip quota threshold checks for CLI requests.
- Updated `getNextForFamily` filter logic to allow CLI requests to proceed regardless of Antigravity quota status.

## Verification
Verified locally with a new test case in `src/plugin/accounts.test.ts` and confirmed via debug logs that `gemini-cli` requests now proceed when Antigravity quota is exhausted.

items.title: agnix/issues #334: feat: Per-client skill validation rules (CR-SK, CL-SK, CP-SK, WS-SK, RC-SK, KR-SK, CX-SK, OC-SK, AMP-SK)
items.content:
## Summary

10 of 14 major AI coding tools now support the Agent Skills standard (SKILL.md). Each tool has different supported frontmatter fields and constraints. agnix currently only validates the universal spec (AS-*) and Claude Code extensions (CC-SK-*), but doesn't warn when client-specific directories contain unsupported fields.

## Problem

A SKILL.md in `.cursor/skills/` with `context: fork` will pass validation, but Cursor doesn't support that field. Users get no warning that their skill won't work as expected in the target tool.

## Research

See `knowledge-base/agent-docs/skills-in-other-tools.md` for the full 46-source research covering all 14 tools.

### Client-Specific Field Support Matrix

| Field | Claude Code | Cursor | Others |
|-------|------------|--------|--------|
| `disable-model-invocation` | Yes | Yes | No |
| `user-invocable` | Yes | No | No |
| `model` | Yes | No | No |
| `context` (fork) | Yes | No | No |
| `agent` | Yes | No | No |
| `hooks` | Yes | No | No |
| `argument-hint` | Yes | No | No |

### Tools that support Agent Skills SKILL.md

Claude Code, Cursor, Cline, VS Code/Copilot, Codex CLI, OpenCode, Windsurf, Amp, Kiro, Roo Code

### Skill directory conventions per tool

| Tool | Primary Path |
|------|-------------|
| Claude Code | `.claude/skills/` |
| Cursor | `.cursor/skills/` |
| Cline | `.cline/skills/` |
| Copilot | `.github/skills/` |
| Codex CLI | `.agents/skills/` |
| OpenCode | `.opencode/skills/` |
| Windsurf | `.windsurf/skills/` |
| Amp | `.agents/skills/` |
| Kiro | `.kiro/skills/` |
| Roo Code | `.roo/skills/` |

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Detection infrastructure

- Extend `detect_file_type()` to distinguish skill directories by parent path
- Add variants or context to `FileType::Skill` so validators know the target client
- Alternative: pass directory context into validators without changing FileType enum

### Phase 2: Per-client skill rules

Add new rule categories and rules to both `rules.json` and `VALIDATION-RULES.md`:

**Per-client unsupported field warnings** (one rule per client that uses SKILL.md):
- `CR-SK-001`: Cursor skill uses unsupported field (warn on `user-invocable`, `model`, `context`, `agent`, `hooks`, `argument-hint`)
- `CL-SK-001`: Cline skill uses unsupported field
- `CP-SK-001`: Copilot skill uses unsupported field
- `CX-SK-001`: Codex skill uses unsupported field
- `OC-SK-001`: OpenCode skill uses unsupported field
- `WS-SK-001`: Windsurf skill uses unsupported field
- `KR-SK-001`: Kiro skill uses unsupported field
- `AMP-SK-001`: Amp skill uses unsupported field
- `RC-SK-001`: Roo Code skill uses unsupported field

**Cross-platform portability rule**:
- `XP-SK-001`: Skill uses client-specific features (flags non-universal fields with which clients don't support them)

### Phase 3: Validator implementation

- Add per-client skill validator that checks fields against the supported set for each tool
- Wire into `ValidatorRegistry` with appropriate `FileType` mapping
- Add auto-fix suggestions where applicable (e.g., remove unsupported field)

### Phase 4: Tests

- Add test fixtures for each client's skill directory
- Test that unsupported fields trigger warnings
- Test that universal-only skills pass without warnings
- Test portability rule

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Skills in `.cursor/skills/` with Claude Code-only fields trigger CR-SK-001 warning
- [ ] Skills in `.cline/skills/` with Claude Code-only fields trigger CL-SK-001 warning
- [ ] Same pattern for all 9 non-Claude clients
- [ ] XP-SK-001 fires for any skill using non-universal fields (regardless of directory)
- [ ] Universal-only skills pass without warnings in any client directory
- [ ] All new rules in both `rules.json` and `VALIDATION-RULES.md`
- [ ] Tests for all new rules
- [ ] Existing tests still pass

items.title: opencode/issues #12626: [FEATURE]: Agent-driven Selective Context Management via Block IDs
items.content:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

**Describe the enhancement you want to request**

### **Disclaimer**
I am a user of Opencode and do not have a background in TypeScript or the project's internal codebase. I am proposing this as a functional enhancement rather than a technical implementation plan.

# **1. The Problem**
Currently, Opencode manages long conversations using automatic cleanup (pruning and compaction). While this is helpful for staying within token limits, it is a "system-level" decision that doesn't always align with the actual progress of the task. 

For example, the system might automatically delete an important piece of code I read earlier that the agent still needs, or it might keep thousands of tokens of useless error logs that have already been resolved, simply because they are "recent."

# **2. The Proposed Idea: Agent-driven Context Management**
I suggest giving the AI agent the ability to **actively manage its own memory** using a block-based system:

- **Visible Block IDs**: Every significant part of the conversation (a user message, a large tool output, a reasoning block) should be assigned a unique ID that the agent can see.
- **Agent Control**: Allow the agent to issue commands to manage these blocks. For instance:
    - **Discard**: The agent can decide that a specific block (like a long, failed build log) is no longer useful and should be removed from its context.
    - **Summarize**: The agent can choose to replace a massive block of data with a short summary it generates itself.
    - **Pin**: The agent can mark a specific block as "critical" so that the automatic cleanup system never deletes it.

# **3. Integration with Session Reversion (Rollback)**
Opencode already has a powerful "Revert" feature. It is critical that this new memory management system is integrated with it:
- **Consistent Rollback**: If a user reverts the session to a previous message, any "Discard" or "Summarize" actions taken by the agent *after* that point should also be automatically undone. 
- **Memory Sync**: The agent's memory (the state of which blocks are hidden or summarized) must stay perfectly in sync with the conversation history. If we go back in time, the agent should "regain" the full context that was available at that moment.

# **4. Benefits**
- **Smarter Context**: The agent knows better than the system which information is truly "finished" and which is "ongoing."
- **Efficiency**: By proactively cleaning up resolved issues, the agent can keep the conversation focused and high-quality for much longer.
- **Reliability**: Ensuring that memory management respects rollbacks will prevent the agent from being "confused" by missing information that it previously discarded in a future that no longer exists.

# Similar Issues

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/7459
https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/9896
https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/8932

- **Smarter Context**: The agent knows better than the system which information is truly "finished" and which is "ongoing."
- **Efficiency**: By proactively cleaning up resolved issues, the agent can keep the conversation focused and high-quality for much longer.
- **Reliability**: Ensuring that memory management respects rollbacks will prevent the agent from being "confused" by missing information that it previously discarded in a future that no longer exists.

https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/9896

items.title: clepho/issues #53: Daemon uses separate, divergent LLM implementation
items.content:
## Problem

`daemon.rs:call_llm_for_description()` is a completely separate LLM implementation that bypasses the provider system:

- **Only speaks OpenAI-compatible API** — ignores the provider config setting, so won't work with Anthropic or Ollama
- **Sends raw file bytes without resize** — modern camera files can be 30MB+, resulting in huge base64 payloads
- **Uses a different default prompt** that omits the `TAGS:` instruction
- **Saves description only** — no tags, no embeddings (uses `save_photo_description_by_id` instead of `save_llm_result`)
- **Processes sequentially** with a hardcoded 500ms sleep instead of using `LlmQueue`

## Impact

Daemon-processed photos are second-class citizens: no tags, no embeddings for semantic search, potentially enormous API payloads, and only works with OpenAI-compatible providers.

## Suggested Fix

Refactor the daemon to use `LlmClient`/`LlmQueue` with `describe_and_tag_image()`. This gives multi-provider support, image resize, tags, and embeddings for free.

items.title: pulse-multi-agent-platform/issues #25: Unified API Hub for Free LLM Providers
items.content:
🚀 Feature Request: Unified API Hub for Free LLM Providers

📋 Summary

Build a centralized API hub that provides a single, unified interface to multiple free LLM providers with automatic failover when quota limits are reached.

🎯 Objectives

  • Single API Interface: One endpoint to rule them all
  • Automatic Failover: Seamlessly switch providers when quotas are exhausted
  • Quota Management: Track and manage rate limits across all providers
  • Provider Agnostic: Abstract away provider-specific implementations
  • High Availability: Ensure continuous service through intelligent routing

🔍 Research & Provider Analysis

Target Free LLM Providers

  1. Groq - Fast inference, generous free tier
  2. Together AI - Multiple open-source models, free tier available
  3. Hugging Face Inference API - Various models, rate-limited free tier
  4. Google Gemini - Free tier with good quotas
  5. Cohere - Trial/free tier available
  6. Anthropic Claude - Limited free tier via API
  7. OpenRouter - Aggregator with some free models
  8. Replicate - Pay-per-use with free credits
  9. DeepInfra - Free tier for various models
  10. Mistral AI - Free tier available

Key Challenges

  • ❌ Different API formats (OpenAI-compatible vs proprietary)
  • ❌ Varying rate limits and quota structures
  • ❌ Different authentication mechanisms
  • ❌ Model capability differences
  • ❌ Response format inconsistencies
  • ❌ Complex error handling and failover logic

🏗️ Architecture Design

System Components

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     API Gateway Layer                    │
│          (Single Unified Endpoint + Auth)               │
└─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                      │
┌─────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Intelligent Router                      │
│        (Provider Selection + Failover Logic)            │
└─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────┘
                      │
        ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
        │             │             │
┌───────▼──────┐ ┌───▼──────┐ ┌───▼──────┐
│   Quota      │ │ Request  │ │ Response │
│  Manager     │ │Translator│ │Normalizer│
└──────────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘
        │             │             │
        └─────────────┼─────────────┘
                      │
        ┌─────────────┼─────────────┐
        │             │             │
┌───────▼──────┐ ┌───▼──────┐ ┌───▼──────┐
│   Provider   │ │ Provider │ │ Provider │
│      A       │ │     B    │ │     C    │
│   (Groq)     │ │(Together)│ │ (Gemini) │
└──────────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────┘

Core Components

1. API Gateway Layer

  • Single unified endpoint for clients
  • Request authentication and validation
  • Request routing to appropriate handler
  • OpenAPI documentation

2. Model Registry/Configuration

Database/config storing:

  • Provider details (API keys, endpoints)
  • Model capabilities and mappings
  • Quota limits and current usage
  • Priority/fallback order
  • Health status

3. Quota Manager

  • Tracks usage per provider (requests/min, tokens/day)
  • Monitors rate limits in real-time
  • Implements circuit breaker pattern
  • Auto-resets counters based on provider windows
  • Provides availability status to router

4. Intelligent Router

Selects available provider based on:

  • Current quota status
  • Model availability/compatibility
  • Provider priority configuration
  • Response time/reliability metrics
  • Implements fallback chain logic

5. Request Translator

  • Converts unified API format to provider-specific format
  • Maps model names to provider equivalents
  • Handles provider-specific parameters
  • Normalizes input across different schemas

6. Response Normalizer

  • Standardizes responses from different providers
  • Uniform error format
  • Consistent streaming format (SSE)
  • Token usage normalization

7. Monitoring & Logging

  • Track usage statistics per provider
  • Log errors and fallback events
  • Performance metrics and latency tracking
  • Alert on quota thresholds
  • Health check dashboard

💻 Technology Stack

Backend Framework

Primary: Python with FastAPI

  • ✅ Async support for concurrent requests
  • ✅ Built-in OpenAPI documentation
  • ✅ Easy integration with LLM libraries
  • ✅ Type hints and validation with Pydantic

Alternative: Node.js with Express

Database & Caching

Redis for:

  • Quota counters (fast atomic increments)
  • Rate limiting (sliding window)
  • Response caching
  • Provider health status

PostgreSQL/SQLite for:

  • Configuration storage
  • API key management
  • Usage history and analytics
  • Audit logs

Queue System (Optional but Recommended)

  • Celery or Redis Queue
  • Async processing and retry logic
  • Request queuing when all providers rate-limited

Additional Libraries

# Core dependencies
fastapi>=0.104.0
uvicorn[standard]>=0.24.0
pydantic>=2.0.0
httpx>=0.25.0  # Async HTTP client

# Database & Caching
redis>=5.0.0
sqlalchemy>=2.0.0
alembic>=1.12.0

# LLM Integrations
openai>=1.0.0
anthropic>=0.7.0
google-generativeai>=0.3.0
cohere>=4.0.0

# Monitoring
prometheus-client>=0.18.0
python-json-logger>=2.0.0

🔌 Unified API Design

Endpoint Structure

POST /v1/chat/completions
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

Request Format

{
  "model": "gpt-3.5-turbo-equivalent",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}
  ],
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "max_tokens": 1000,
  "stream": false,
  "provider": "groq"  // Optional: force specific provider
}

Response Format

{
  "id": "chatcmpl-123",
  "object": "chat.completion",
  "created": 1677652288,
  "model": "llama-3.1-70b",
  "provider": "groq",
  "choices": [{
    "index": 0,
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Hello! How can I help you today?"
    },
    "finish_reason": "stop"
  }],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 10,
    "completion_tokens": 9,
    "total_tokens": 19
  }
}

🔄 Failover Logic Flow

1. Request received at API Gateway
   ↓
2. Authenticate & validate request
   ↓
3. Check if specific provider requested
   ↓
4. If not → Consult Quota Manager for available providers
   ↓
5. Router selects provider based on:
   - Quota availability ✓
   - Priority order ✓
   - Model compatibility ✓
   - Recent performance ✓
   ↓
6. Attempt request to Provider A
   ↓
7. Response received?
   ├─ YES → Normalize response → Return to client ✓
   │
   └─ NO → Check error type:
       ├─ 429 (Quota exceeded) → Mark exhausted → Next provider
       ├─ 5xx (Server error) → Increment failure count → Next provider
       ├─ Network timeout → Next provider
       └─ 4xx (Client error) → Return error to client ✗
   ↓
8. Retry with Provider B (repeat step 6-7)
   ↓
9. Continue until:
   - Success ✓
   - All providers exhausted ✗
   ↓
10. Return unified response or aggregated error

⚙️ Configuration Example

Provider Configuration (YAML)

providers:
  - name: groq
    enabled: true
    priority: 1
    api_key: ${GROQ_API_KEY}
    endpoint: https://api.groq.com/openai/v1/chat/completions
    format: openai
    timeout: 30
    quotas:
      requests_per_minute: 30
      requests_per_day: 14400
      tokens_per_minute: 7000
      tokens_per_day: null
    models:
      - id: llama-3.1-70b
        alias: gpt-3.5-turbo-equivalent
        context_window: 8192
      - id: mixtral-8x7b
        alias: mixtral-medium
        context_window: 32768
    health_check:
      enabled: true
      interval: 300  # seconds
      
  - name: together
    enabled: true
    priority: 2
    api_key: ${TOGETHER_API_KEY}
    endpoint: https://api.together.xyz/v1/chat/completions
    format: openai
    timeout: 45
    quotas:
      requests_per_minute: 60
      requests_per_day: null
      tokens_per_minute: null
      tokens_per_day: 1000000
    models:
      - id: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-Turbo
        alias: llama-70b
        context_window: 8192
      - id: mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1
        alias: mixtral-medium
        context_window: 32768
        
  - name: gemini
    enabled: true
    priority: 3
    api_key: ${GOOGLE_API_KEY}
    endpoint: https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta
    format: google
    timeout: 60
    quotas:
      requests_per_minute: 60
      requests_per_day: 1500
      tokens_per_minute: 32000
    models:
      - id: gemini-1.5-flash
        alias: gemini-flash
        context_window: 1000000

# Global settings
settings:
  default_model: gpt-3.5-turbo-equivalent
  max_retries: 3
  retry_delay: 1.0  # seconds
  circuit_breaker:
    failure_threshold: 5
    recovery_timeout: 60
    half_open_requests: 3
  cache:
    enabled: true
    ttl: 3600
    max_size: 1000

📊 Implementation Phases

Phase 1: MVP (Weeks 1-2)

Goal: Basic working prototype

  • [ ] Set up FastAPI project structure
  • [ ] Implement basic API gateway with authentication
  • [ ] Integrate 2-3 providers (Groq, Together AI, Gemini)
  • [ ] Simple round-robin failover logic
  • [ ] In-memory quota tracking
  • [ ] Basic error handling
  • [ ] Unit tests for core components

Deliverables:

  • Working API endpoint
  • Basic provider adapters
  • Simple configuration file
  • README with setup instructions

Phase 2: Enhanced Features (Weeks 3-4)

Goal: Production-ready quota management

  • [ ] PostgreSQL for configuration storage
  • [ ] Intelligent routing based on model capabilities
  • [ ] Add 3-4 more providers
  • [ ] Implement circuit breaker pattern
  • [ ] Request/Response normalization layer
  • [ ] Comprehensive error mapping
  • [ ] Integration tests

Deliverables:

  • Redis-based quota manager
  • Database schema and migrations
  • Enhanced routing logic
  • API documentation (OpenAPI)

Phase 3: Production Ready (Weeks 5-6)

Goal: Deployment and monitoring

  • [ ] Monitoring and analytics dashboard
  • [ ] Rate limiting per client API key
  • [ ] Response caching layer
  • [ ] Admin panel for configuration
  • [ ] Docker containerization
  • [ ] Health check endpoints
  • [ ] Logging and metrics (Prometheus)
  • [ ] Load testing and optimization

Deliverables:

  • Docker Compose setup
  • Monitoring dashboard
  • Admin interface
  • Deployment documentation
  • Performance benchmarks

Phase 4: Advanced Features (Weeks 7-8)

Goal: Optimization and scaling

  • [ ] Load balancing across provider instances
  • [ ] A/B testing framework for providers
  • [ ] Custom model routing rules
  • [ ] Request queuing system
  • [ ] API key rotation support
  • [ ] Cost tracking and analytics
  • [ ] Webhook notifications for quota alerts
  • [ ] Multi-region deployment support

Deliverables:

  • Advanced routing engine

✨ Key Features to Implement

1. Health Checks

  • Periodic provider availability checks (every 5 minutes)
  • Automatic provider disabling on consecutive failures
  • Health status API endpoint
  • Notification on provider downtime

2. Circuit Breaker

  • Temporarily disable failing providers
  • Configurable failure threshold
  • Automatic recovery attempts
  • Half-open state for gradual recovery

3. Retry Logic

  • Exponential backoff for transient errors
  • Configurable max retry attempts
  • Different retry strategies per error type
  • Request deduplication

4. Streaming Support

  • Handle Server-Sent Events (SSE) from multiple providers
  • Unified streaming interface
  • Stream buffering and error recovery
  • Connection timeout handling

5. Request Queuing

  • Queue requests when all providers rate-limited
  • Priority queue for different client tiers
  • Queue size limits and overflow handling
  • Estimated wait time calculation

6. API Key Rotation

  • Automatic rotation on quota exhaustion
  • Key health tracking

7. Usage Analytics

🔌 Unified API Design

Endpoint Structure

POST /v1/chat/completions
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY

Request Format

{
  "model": "gpt-3.5-turbo-equivalent",
  "messages": [
    {"role": "system", "content": "You are a helpful assistant."},
    {"role": "user", "content": "Hello!"}
  ],
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "max_tokens": 1000,
  "stream": false,
  "provider": "groq"  // Optional: force specific provider
}

Response Format

{
  "id": "chatcmpl-123",
  "object": "chat.completion",
  "created": 1677652288,
  "model": "llama-3.1-70b",
  "provider": "groq",
  "choices": [{
    "index": 0,
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": "Hello! How can I help you today?"
    },
    "finish_reason": "stop"
  }],
  "usage": {
    "prompt_tokens": 10,
    "completion_tokens": 9,
    "total_tokens": 19
  }
}

🔄 Failover Logic Flow

1. Request received at API Gateway
   ↓
2. Authenticate & validate request
   ↓
3. Check if specific provider requested
   ↓
4. If not → Consult Quota Manager for available providers
   ↓
5. Router selects provider based on:
   - Quota availability ✓
   - Priority order ✓
   - Model compatibility ✓
   - Recent performance ✓
   ↓
6. Attempt request to Provider A
   ↓
7. Response received?
   ├─ YES → Normalize response → Return to client ✓
   │
   └─ NO → Check error type:
       ├─ 429 (Quota exceeded) → Mark exhausted → Next provider
       ├─ 5xx (Server error) → Increment failure count → Next provider
       ├─ Network timeout → Next provider
       └─ 4xx (Client error) → Return error to client ✗
   ↓
8. Retry with Provider B (repeat step 6-7)
   ↓
9. Continue until:
   - Success ✓
   - All providers exhausted ✗
   ↓
10. Return unified response or aggregated error

raw.body:
I have been working on a JavaScript video player.

document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {

  String.prototype.timeFormat = function() {
    let sec = parseInt(this, 10);
    let h = Math.floor(sec / 3600);
    let m = Math.floor((sec % 3600) / 60);
    let s = sec % 60;
    if (h < 10) h = '0' + h;
    if (m < 10) m = '0' + m;
    if (s < 10) s = '0' + s;
    return h > 0 ? `${h}:${m}:${s}` : `${m}:${s}`;
  };

  function toggleFullScreen(elem) {
    if (!document.fullscreenElement) {
      elem.requestFullscreen?.() || elem.webkitRequestFullscreen?.() || elem.msRequestFullscreen?.();
    } else {
      document.exitFullscreen?.() || document.webkitExitFullscreen?.() || document.msExitFullscreen?.();
    }
  }

  document.querySelectorAll('.video-container').forEach(container => {
    const video = container.querySelector('video');
    const poster = container.querySelector('.poster');
    const spinner = container.querySelector('.loading-spinner');
    const playBtn = container.querySelector('input[name="play-pause"]');
    const progressBar = container.querySelector('.progress-bar');
    const progress = container.querySelector('.progress');
    const currentTimeEl = container.querySelector('.current-time');
    const durationEl = container.querySelector('.duration');
    const volumeSlider = container.querySelector('.volume-slider');
    const muteToggle = container.querySelector('.mute-toggle');
    const muteCheckbox = muteToggle.querySelector('input[type="checkbox"]');
    const rateDisplay = container.querySelector('.rate_display');
    const fullscreenBtn = container.querySelector('input[name="screen-toggler"]');
    const rateOptions = container.querySelectorAll('.playback-rate ul li');

    let manualPaused = false;
    let isTryingToPlay = false;

    function showSpinner() {
      spinner.style.opacity = 1;
    }

    function hideSpinner() {
      spinner.style.opacity = 0;
    }

    function updatePlayPause() {
      if (video.paused) {
        playBtn.value = 'Play';
        playBtn.classList.add('play');
        playBtn.classList.remove('pause');
      } else {
        playBtn.value = 'Pause';
        playBtn.classList.remove('play');
        playBtn.classList.add('pause');
      }
    }

    function updateProgress() {
      const dur = isFinite(video.duration) ? video.duration : 0;
      const cur = isFinite(video.currentTime) ? video.currentTime : 0;
      const percent = dur > 0 ? (cur / dur) * 100 : 0;
      progress.style.width = percent + '%';
      currentTimeEl.textContent = Math.round(cur).toString().timeFormat();
      durationEl.textContent = dur > 0 ? Math.round(dur).toString().timeFormat() : '--:--';
    }

    async function attemptPlay() {
      if (manualPaused || isTryingToPlay) return;
      isTryingToPlay = true;
      showSpinner();
      try {
        await video.play();
      } catch {}
      hideSpinner();
      isTryingToPlay = false;
      updatePlayPause();
    }

    playBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
      manualPaused = !video.paused;
      if (!manualPaused) {
        poster.style.display = 'none';
        attemptPlay();
      } else {
        video.pause();
      }
    });

    volumeSlider.addEventListener('input', () => {
      video.volume = volumeSlider.value;
      video.muted = video.volume === 0;
      muteCheckbox.checked = video.muted;
      muteToggle.classList.toggle('muted', video.muted);
    });

    muteToggle.addEventListener('click', () => {
      video.muted = muteCheckbox.checked;
      muteToggle.classList.toggle('muted', video.muted);
    });

    progressBar.addEventListener('click', e => {
      const rect = progressBar.getBoundingClientRect();
      const dur = isFinite(video.duration) && video.duration > 0 ? video.duration : 100;
      video.currentTime = ((e.clientX - rect.left) / rect.width) * dur;
      updateProgress();
      attemptPlay();
    });

    fullscreenBtn.addEventListener('click', () => {
      container.classList.toggle('fullscreen');
      fullscreenBtn.classList.toggle('exit');
      toggleFullScreen(document.body);
    });

    document.addEventListener('fullscreenchange', () => {
      if (!document.fullscreenElement) {
        container.classList.remove('fullscreen');
        fullscreenBtn.classList.remove('exit');
      }
    });

    rateOptions.forEach(opt => {
      opt.addEventListener('click', () => {
        video.playbackRate = parseFloat(opt.dataset.rate);
        rateDisplay.textContent = video.playbackRate === 1 ? 'Normal' : video.playbackRate + 'x';
      });
    });

    video.addEventListener('loadedmetadata', updateProgress);
    video.addEventListener('timeupdate', updateProgress);
    video.addEventListener('waiting', showSpinner);
    video.addEventListener('stalled', showSpinner);
    video.addEventListener('seeking', showSpinner);
    video.addEventListener('playing', () => {
      hideSpinner();
      updatePlayPause();
    });
    video.addEventListener('canplay', () => {
      hideSpinner();
      updatePlayPause();
    });
    video.addEventListener('pause', updatePlayPause);
    video.addEventListener('ended', updatePlayPause);
    video.addEventListener('seeked', () => {
      updateProgress();
      if (!manualPaused) attemptPlay();
      updatePlayPause();
    });
  });
});

items.content:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I will write this issue in English (see our [Language Policy](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-opencode/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#language-policy))
- [x] I have searched existing issues to avoid duplicates
- [x] I am using the latest version of oh-my-opencode
- [x] I have read the [documentation](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-opencode#readme) or asked an AI coding agent with this project's GitHub URL loaded and couldn't find the answer

### Bug Description

Title: start-work can spawn concurrent vitest workers causing memory exhaustion on 16GB machines

## Summary
Running `/start-work` with parallel waves can spawn multiple `vitest` Node processes at the same time.
On a 16GB Mac, this leads to sustained memory pressure, swap growth, and unstable execution.

## Impact
- High memory usage (multiple `node (vitest N)` processes)
- Significant swap growth
- CI-like local validation becomes unreliable
- Increased flaky behavior due to resource contention

## Environment
- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon)
- RAM: 16GB
- Branch: `dev`
- Date observed: 2026-02-07
- Repo: `oh-my-opencode`

## Reproduction Steps
1. Prepare a plan with parallel waves (including multiple test-related tasks).
2. Run `/start-work` on that plan.
3. Observe process list / Activity Monitor:
   - Multiple `node (vitest X)` processes running concurrently.
4. Observe memory/swap:
   - Memory pressure stays high
   - Swap keeps increasing

## Expected Behavior
- At most one `memory-heavy` test workload should run at a time.
- `start-work` should avoid watch-mode semantics in automated execution.
- When pressure threshold is exceeded, scheduler should stop dispatching new heavy tasks and degrade to serial mode.

## Actual Behavior
- Multiple memory-heavy test processes are dispatched concurrently.
- No effective circuit-breaker or mutex for heavy workloads.
- System enters swap pressure and execution quality degrades.

## Evidence
- Activity Monitor screenshot showing concurrent `node (vitest N)` processes and high memory use
- Command logs from plan execution (can attach if needed)

## Proposed Fix
1. Add scheduler guardrails in `/start-work`:
   - `max_parallel=2`
   - `memory-heavy` mutex = 1
2. Enforce non-watch test semantics in automation:
   - use `vitest run` (not `vitest` watch)
3. Add circuit breaker:
   - trigger when `mem > 85%` or `swap > 25%`
   - pause new heavy dispatch; queue in FIFO
4. Add recovery condition:
   - resume parallel only after `mem < 70%` sustained for 30s
5. Add policy docs in:
   - `AGENTS.md`
   - `.sisyphus` plan/start-work templates

## Acceptance Criteria
- Reproduction scenario no longer causes multiple concurrent heavy test processes.
- Under pressure, scheduler enters degraded serial mode automatically.
- Recovery path is logged and auditable.


### Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a 16GB macOS machine and open this repository on branch `dev`.
2. Prepare a work plan that contains parallel waves with multiple test-related tasks.
3. Run `/start-work` with that plan.
4. Observe Activity Monitor (or `ps`) during execution.
5. Confirm multiple `node (vitest X)` processes are running at the same time.
6. Observe memory pressure and swap usage increasing continuously.


### Expected Behavior

`/start-work` should enforce scheduling guardrails:
- No watch-mode test process in automated execution.
- At most one memory-heavy test workload at a time.
- Circuit breaker pauses new heavy dispatch under memory pressure.
- Scheduler degrades to serial mode until recovery conditions are met.


### Actual Behavior

`/start-work` dispatches multiple memory-heavy test workloads concurrently.
This spawns several `node (vitest X)` processes, causing high memory pressure and continuous swap growth on a 16GB machine.

items.title: openchamber/issues #349: [Feature Request] Desktop: Multi-window support (each window can target a different server)
items.content:
### What should we add/change?

#### Problem / Motivation
Right now the desktop app effectively works as a single “workspace”: if I switch the connected server (local vs remote), it changes the context for the whole app. This makes it hard to work with *multiple OpenCode/OpenChamber backends at the same time*.

I often run:
- a local server (fast iteration)
- a remote server (VPS / homelab)
and I want to keep them open side-by-side without constantly switching the active server.

#### Requested Feature
Add **multi-window support** to the desktop app so I can:
- open a **new window**
- select a different **server / instance** for that window
- run sessions and terminals in parallel across multiple servers

Concretely: I’d like to have Window A connected to Server A, and Window B connected to Server B (independent state and streams).

#### UX Proposal
- Menu item: **File → New Window** (and a shortcut like `⌘⇧N` or similar)
- On new window open:
  - either prompt to pick a server profile
  - or open with last-used server and allow changing it from the header/settings
- Show which server the window is connected to (window title or a small badge in the UI)

Optional (nice-to-have, but not required):
- “Duplicate Window” (same server as current window)
- Remember last server per window across restarts

#### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] I can open multiple desktop windows.
- [ ] Each window can target a different server/instance independently.
- [ ] Sessions list, chat, terminal, and streaming in one window do not interfere with the other window.
- [ ] The UI makes it obvious which server a given window is connected to.

#### Why this matters
This would enable a workflow similar to Terminal apps: multiple windows/tabs for different environments (local, staging, remote, etc.). It’s especially useful when comparing behavior, debugging remote-only issues, or just keeping long-running sessions on a remote server while iterating locally.


### Extra context (optional)

In the desktop settings menu almost no components have styles for when focus-visible should be showing - i.e keyboard navigation.

Add handlers to all entry points: `bot.js`, `opencode-bot.js`, `teams-bot.js`, `teams-opencode-bot.js`, `discord-bot.js`, `discord-opencode-bot.js`, `sprite-bot.js`.

- All `src/*-bot.js` entry points

## Severity
High — silent crashes

items.title: Workflows/issues #1322: [Follow-up] Update docs/verification-concerns-1307.md: Ensure  (PR #1316)
items.content:
# Address Remaining Verification Gaps from PR #1316

## Why
PR #1316 addressed issue #1315, but verification returned a **CONCERNS** verdict due to remaining gaps: high-severity concerns are not fully traceable to concrete resolutions/decisions with repo-local evidence, LLM invocation paths still lack tests that assert config/metadata propagation (and logging on fallback), model classification logic can misclassify names, and some workflows still reference older `actions/upload-artifact` versions. This follow-up issue closes those gaps with explicit documentation, evidence, tests, and minimal safe refactors.

## Source
- Original PR: #1316
- Parent issue: #1315

## Tasks

### Documentation & Traceability
- [ ] Add resolution links and summaries to each high-severity concern in `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md` that was resolved by code changes
- [ ] Add explicit `DECISIONS.md` references to each high-severity concern in `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md` that was resolved by architectural decision
- [ ] Add per-concern evidence links pointing to repo-local verification artifacts for each high-severity concern in `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md`
- [ ] Add dated entry to `DECISIONS.md` for the "missing artifacts" concern including decision statement, rationale, date (ISO format), and evidence link

### Re-verification Evidence Artifacts
- [ ] Create `docs/reverification/README.md` explaining how evidence files are produced and what they contain
- [ ] Create a dated re-verification evidence markdown file under `docs/reverification/` with clearly labeled sections for each high-severity concern
- [ ] Update `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md` to link to the dated re-verification evidence file for each high-severity concern

### LLM Invocation Testing
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_pr_verifier.py` that mock `client.invoke` and assert config/metadata propagation for all LLM invocation call sites
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_followup_issue_generator.py` that mock `client.invoke` and assert config/metadata propagation for all LLM invocation call sites
- [ ] Add test in `tests/test_followup_issue_generator.py` that forces the `TypeError` path and asserts warning/error log emission with exception info and fallback phrase

### Model Classification Refactoring
- [ ] Refactor `tools/langchain_client._is_reasoning_model` to use a start-anchored regex pattern that matches only `o` followed by digits
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_langchain_client.py` covering both intended model names (`o1`, `o3`, `o123`) and edge cases (`o-mini`, `gpt-4o`, `foo`, `O1`) for `_is_reasoning_model` classification

### Logging Improvements
- [ ] Update `followup_issue_generator.py` `_invoke_llm` to log warning/error when `TypeError` is raised, including exception text and explicit phrase indicating config/metadata fallback

## Deferred Tasks (Requires Human)
- [ ] **Manual:** Update all `.github/workflows/*.yml` files to use `actions/upload-artifact@v7` instead of older versions (v3/v4/v5/v6) and adjust any related inputs for v7 compatibility

## Acceptance Criteria

### Documentation Traceability
- [ ] In `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md`, every high-severity concern entry includes a `Resolution:` field with at least one GitHub PR URL (containing `/pull/`) OR commit URL (containing `/commit/`) plus a non-empty `Summary:` line
- [ ] In `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md`, every high-severity concern entry that was resolved by architectural decision includes a `Decision:` field that references a `DECISIONS.md` entry by anchor or heading text
- [ ] In `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md`, every high-severity concern entry contains an `Evidence:` field with a relative link to a repo-local file path under `docs/reverification/`
- [ ] `DECISIONS.md` contains a dated entry for the "missing artifacts" concern with all of:
  - A one-sentence `Decision` statement
  - A `Rationale` section with at least one bullet or paragraph
  - A `Date:` field in ISO format `YYYY-MM-DD`
  - An `Evidence:` link to a repo-local file under `docs/reverification/`

### Re-verification Evidence
- [ ] A repo-local re-verification evidence file exists at `docs/reverification/<YYYY-MM-DD>-*.md` where the filename contains a date prefix in `YYYY-MM-DD` format
- [ ] `docs/reverification/README.md` exists and describes how the evidence file is produced or what it contains
- [ ] `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md` links to the dated `docs/reverification` evidence file and each high-severity concern's `Evidence:` link points to a specific section within that file (markdown anchor) or to a per-concern evidence file under `docs/reverification/`

### LLM Invocation Tests - pr_verifier.py
- [ ] `tests/test_pr_verifier.py` contains at least one test that patches/mocks the underlying LLM client's `invoke` method used by `pr_verifier.py`
- [ ] The test asserts that the invocation receives the constructed config/metadata argument (not just that `_build_llm_config` returns it)
- [ ] The test covers every call site in `pr_verifier.py` that triggers an LLM invocation

### LLM Invocation Tests - followup_issue_generator.py
- [ ] `tests/test_followup_issue_generator.py` contains at least one test that patches/mocks the underlying LLM client's `invoke` method used by `followup_issue_generator.py`
- [ ] The test asserts that `_invoke_llm` passes the constructed config/metadata argument through to `invoke`
- [ ] The test covers every call site in `followup_issue_generator.py` that triggers an LLM invocation
- [ ] `tests/test_followup_issue_generator.py` includes a test that forces the `TypeError` path by mocking `invoke` to raise `TypeError` when called with config/metadata
- [ ] The `TypeError` test asserts a warning/error log record is emitted containing:
  - The exception text or repr
  - An explicit phrase indicating config/metadata fallback occurred
- [ ] The `TypeError` test verifies that a second invocation without config/metadata occurs (fallback behavior preserved)

### Model Classification
- [ ] `tools/langchain_client._is_reasoning_model` uses a regex anchored at the start that matches only model names beginning with `o` followed immediately by one or more digits (e.g., `^o\d+`)
- [ ] `tools/langchain_client._is_reasoning_model` does not match names like `o-mini`
- [ ] `tests/test_langchain_client.py` includes explicit cases asserting `_is_reasoning_model` returns `True` for: `o1`, `o3`, `o123`
- [ ] `tests/test_langchain_client.py` includes explicit cases asserting `_is_reasoning_model` returns `False` for: `o-mini`, `gpt-4o`, `foo`, `O1`

### Logging
- [ ] `followup_issue_generator.py` `_invoke_llm` logs a warning or error when a `TypeError` is raised due to passing config/metadata to a client that does not accept it
- [ ] The log message includes both:
  - The exception text (or repr)
  - An explicit phrase indicating config/metadata was not passed due to fallback

### Test Suite
- [ ] All newly added tests in `tests/test_pr_verifier.py`, `tests/test_followup_issue_generator.py`, and `tests/test_langchain_client.py` pass individually when run with pytest
- [ ] No new test failures are introduced in existing test files when running the full test suite

## Implementation Notes

### Documentation traceability
- In `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md`, standardize each high-severity concern to include fields like `Resolution:` (PR/commit link) + `Summary:` or `Decision:` (link to `DECISIONS.md` entry), plus `Evidence:` pointing to a repo-local `docs/` path.
- Prefer relative links (e.g., `docs/reverification/2026-02-07-...md#concern-x`) so they work in GitHub UI and remain stable.

### Re-verification evidence artifact
- Add `docs/reverification/README.md` explaining what is captured (commands run, environment assumptions, how to regenerate).
- Add at least one dated evidence markdown file whose filename begins with `YYYY-MM-DD` and contains clearly labeled sections per high-severity concern to support anchored links.

### LLM invocation tests
- Ensure tests validate real invocation paths: patch/mock the actual `client.invoke` used by each module, call the public/entry methods that trigger LLM calls, and assert the invoke args include the constructed config/metadata.
- Cover *all* LLM invocation call sites in `pr_verifier.py` and `followup_issue_generator.py`, not only helper builders.
- For the fallback behavior in `followup_issue_generator.py`, use `caplog` (or equivalent) to assert a warning/error log is emitted, and assert the invoke call happens twice (first with config → `TypeError`, second without config succeeds).

### Model classification
- Update `_is_reasoning_model` to a start-anchored regex such as `r"^o\d+"` and add explicit tests including `O1` to lock down case-sensitivity expectations.

### Workflow changes (manual)
- Keep workflow edits scoped: only bump `actions/upload-artifact` to `@v7` and adjust inputs solely as required for v7 compatibility.
- After manual updates, validate via ripgrep: `rg "actions/upload-artifact@v[3-6]" .github/workflows/` should return no matches.

<details>
<summary>Background (previous attempt context)</summary>

- **Lack of explicit re-verification evidence for high-severity concerns:**
  - Earlier approach referenced workflow artifacts without ensuring repository documentation provided direct evidence.
  - Instead: incorporate embedded test results/artifact files in the repo, or dated repo-local evidence links in `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md` and `DECISIONS.md`.

- **Insufficient tests for verifying metadata propagation in LLM invocation:**
  - Prior iterations only tested the configuration builder (`_build_llm_config`) but not the use of this configuration in actual `client.invoke` calls.
  - Instead: mock/intercept `client.invoke` and assert constructed config/metadata is passed for each invocation path; include coverage for fallback behavior.

</details>

## Critical Rules
1. Do NOT include "Remaining Unchecked Items" or "Iteration Details" sections unless they contain specific, useful failure context
2. Tasks should be concrete actions, not verification concerns restated
3. Acceptance criteria must be testable (not "all concerns addressed")
4. Keep the main body focused - hide background/history in the collapsible section
5. Do NOT include the entire analysis object - only include specific failure contexts from `blockers_to_avoid`

This follow-up issue closes those gaps with explicit documentation, evidence, tests, and minimal safe refactors.

## Source
- Original PR: #1316
- Parent issue: #1315

## Tasks

### Documentation & Traceability
- [ ] Add resolution links and summaries to each high-severity concern in `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md` that was resolved by code changes
- [ ] Add explicit `DECISIONS.md` references to each high-severity concern in `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md` that was resolved by architectural decision
- [ ] Add per-concern evidence links pointing to repo-local verification artifacts for each high-severity concern in `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md`
- [ ] Add dated entry to `DECISIONS.md` for the "missing artifacts" concern including decision statement, rationale, date (ISO format), and evidence link

### Re-verification Evidence Artifacts
- [ ] Create `docs/reverification/README.md` explaining how evidence files are produced and what they contain
- [ ] Create a dated re-verification evidence markdown file under `docs/reverification/` with clearly labeled sections for each high-severity concern
- [ ] Update `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md` to link to the dated re-verification evidence file for each high-severity concern

### LLM Invocation Testing
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_pr_verifier.py` that mock `client.invoke` and assert config/metadata propagation for all LLM invocation call sites
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_followup_issue_generator.py` that mock `client.invoke` and assert config/metadata propagation for all LLM invocation call sites
- [ ] Add test in `tests/test_followup_issue_generator.py` that forces the `TypeError` path and asserts warning/error log emission with exception info and fallback phrase

### Model Classification Refactoring
- [ ] Refactor `tools/langchain_client._is_reasoning_model` to use a start-anchored regex pattern that matches only `o` followed by digits
- [ ] Add unit tests in `tests/test_langchain_client.py` covering both intended model names (`o1`, `o3`, `o123`) and edge cases (`o-mini`, `gpt-4o`, `foo`, `O1`) for `_is_reasoning_model` classification

### Logging Improvements
- [ ] Update `followup_issue_generator.py` `_invoke_llm` to log warning/error when `TypeError` is raised, including exception text and explicit phrase indicating config/metadata fallback

## Deferred Tasks (Requires Human)
- [ ] **Manual:** Update all `.github/workflows/*.yml` files to use `actions/upload-artifact@v7` instead of older versions (v3/v4/v5/v6) and adjust any related inputs for v7 compatibility

## Acceptance Criteria

### Documentation Traceability
- [ ] In `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md`, every high-severity concern entry includes a `Resolution:` field with at least one GitHub PR URL (containing `/pull/`) OR commit URL (containing `/commit/`) plus a non-empty `Summary:` line
- [ ] In `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md`, every high-severity concern entry that was resolved by architectural decision includes a `Decision:` field that references a `DECISIONS.md` entry by anchor or heading text
- [ ] In `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md`, every high-severity concern entry contains an `Evidence:` field with a relative link to a repo-local file path under `docs/reverification/`
- [ ] `DECISIONS.md` contains a dated entry for the "missing artifacts" concern with all of:
  - A one-sentence `Decision` statement
  - A `Rationale` section with at least one bullet or paragraph
  - A `Date:` field in ISO format `YYYY-MM-DD`
  - An `Evidence:` link to a repo-local file under `docs/reverification/`

### Re-verification Evidence
- [ ] A repo-local re-verification evidence file exists at `docs/reverification/<YYYY-MM-DD>-*.md` where the filename contains a date prefix in `YYYY-MM-DD` format
- [ ] `docs/reverification/README.md` exists and describes how the evidence file is produced or what it contains
- [ ] `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md` links to the dated `docs/reverification` evidence file and each high-severity concern's `Evidence:` link points to a specific section within that file (markdown anchor) or to a per-concern evidence file under `docs/reverification/`

### LLM Invocation Tests - pr_verifier.py
- [ ] `tests/test_pr_verifier.py` contains at least one test that patches/mocks the underlying LLM client's `invoke` method used by `pr_verifier.py`
- [ ] The test asserts that the invocation receives the constructed config/metadata argument (not just that `_build_llm_config` returns it)
- [ ] The test covers every call site in `pr_verifier.py` that triggers an LLM invocation

### LLM Invocation Tests - followup_issue_generator.py
- [ ] `tests/test_followup_issue_generator.py` contains at least one test that patches/mocks the underlying LLM client's `invoke` method used by `followup_issue_generator.py`
- [ ] The test asserts that `_invoke_llm` passes the constructed config/metadata argument through to `invoke`
- [ ] The test covers every call site in `followup_issue_generator.py` that triggers an LLM invocation
- [ ] `tests/test_followup_issue_generator.py` includes a test that forces the `TypeError` path by mocking `invoke` to raise `TypeError` when called with config/metadata
- [ ] The `TypeError` test asserts a warning/error log record is emitted containing:
  - The exception text or repr
  - An explicit phrase indicating config/metadata fallback occurred
- [ ] The `TypeError` test verifies that a second invocation without config/metadata occurs (fallback behavior preserved)

### Model Classification
- [ ] `tools/langchain_client._is_reasoning_model` uses a regex anchored at the start that matches only model names beginning with `o` followed immediately by one or more digits (e.g., `^o\d+`)
- [ ] `tools/langchain_client._is_reasoning_model` does not match names like `o-mini`
- [ ] `tests/test_langchain_client.py` includes explicit cases asserting `_is_reasoning_model` returns `True` for: `o1`, `o3`, `o123`
- [ ] `tests/test_langchain_client.py` includes explicit cases asserting `_is_reasoning_model` returns `False` for: `o-mini`, `gpt-4o`, `foo`, `O1`

### Logging
- [ ] `followup_issue_generator.py` `_invoke_llm` logs a warning or error when a `TypeError` is raised due to passing config/metadata to a client that does not accept it
- [ ] The log message includes both:
  - The exception text (or repr)
  - An explicit phrase indicating config/metadata was not passed due to fallback

### Test Suite
- [ ] All newly added tests in `tests/test_pr_verifier.py`, `tests/test_followup_issue_generator.py`, and `tests/test_langchain_client.py` pass individually when run with pytest
- [ ] No new test failures are introduced in existing test files when running the full test suite

## Implementation Notes

### Documentation traceability
- In `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md`, standardize each high-severity concern to include fields like `Resolution:` (PR/commit link) + `Summary:` or `Decision:` (link to `DECISIONS.md` entry), plus `Evidence:` pointing to a repo-local `docs/` path.
- Prefer relative links (e.g., `docs/reverification/2026-02-07-...md#concern-x`) so they work in GitHub UI and remain stable.

### Re-verification evidence artifact
- Add `docs/reverification/README.md` explaining what is captured (commands run, environment assumptions, how to regenerate).
- Add at least one dated evidence markdown file whose filename begins with `YYYY-MM-DD` and contains clearly labeled sections per high-severity concern to support anchored links.

### LLM invocation tests
- Ensure tests validate real invocation paths: patch/mock the actual `client.invoke` used by each module, call the public/entry methods that trigger LLM calls, and assert the invoke args include the constructed config/metadata.
- Cover *all* LLM invocation call sites in `pr_verifier.py` and `followup_issue_generator.py`, not only helper builders.
- For the fallback behavior in `followup_issue_generator.py`, use `caplog` (or equivalent) to assert a warning/error log is emitted, and assert the invoke call happens twice (first with config → `TypeError`, second without config succeeds).

### Model classification
- Update `_is_reasoning_model` to a start-anchored regex such as `r"^o\d+"` and add explicit tests including `O1` to lock down case-sensitivity expectations.

### Workflow changes (manual)
- Keep workflow edits scoped: only bump `actions/upload-artifact` to `@v7` and adjust inputs solely as required for v7 compatibility.
- After manual updates, validate via ripgrep: `rg "actions/upload-artifact@v[3-6]" .github/workflows/` should return no matches.

<details>
<summary>Background (previous attempt context)</summary>

- **Lack of explicit re-verification evidence for high-severity concerns:**
  - Earlier approach referenced workflow artifacts without ensuring repository documentation provided direct evidence.
  - Instead: incorporate embedded test results/artifact files in the repo, or dated repo-local evidence links in `docs/verification-concerns-1307.md` and `DECISIONS.md`.

- **Insufficient tests for verifying metadata propagation in LLM invocation:**
  - Prior iterations only tested the configuration builder (`_build_llm_config`) but not the use of this configuration in actual `client.invoke` calls.
  - Instead: mock/intercept `client.invoke` and assert constructed config/metadata is passed for each invocation path; include coverage for fallback behavior.

</details>

## Critical Rules
1. Do NOT include "Remaining Unchecked Items" or "Iteration Details" sections unless they contain specific, useful failure context
2. Tasks should be concrete actions, not verification concerns restated
3. Acceptance criteria must be testable (not "all concerns addressed")
4. Keep the main body focused - hide background/history in the collapsible section
5. Do NOT include the entire analysis object - only include specific failure contexts from `blockers_to_avoid`

items.title: [FEATURE]: configuration profiles (per‑context setups)
items.content:
### Feature hasn't been suggested before.

- [x] I have verified this feature I'm about to request hasn't been suggested before.

### Describe the enhancement you want to request

I’d like profiles for full configuration sets, not just auth. Specifically, I have multiple ‎`oh-my-opencode` configs that I currently swap manually, and I want to switch between them as profiles.

What I want ￼

- Named profiles (e.g. Personal, Work, Client‑A, Client‑B) that each define:
    1. Active configuration files / directories.
    2. Enabled plugins / subagents / tools.
    3. Default models and providers.
    4. Per‑profile environment (env vars, project roots, workspace layout).
- A fast way to switch profiles:
    1. From the UI (visible selector).
    2. Via a command / keybinding.
- A clear indicator of the current profile so I don’t accidentally run the wrong config.

Why this is useful ￼

- Different contexts (personal, work, different clients) need very different configurations and constraints.

- Today, I have to:
    1.  Manually swap configuration folders / files.
    2.  Restart or reload things to pick up the new setup.
    3.  Remember which config is currently active, which is error‑prone.

- Profiles would:
    1.  Make context switching fast and safe.
    2.  Keep work and personal / client setups clearly separated.
    3.  Encourage focused, minimal configs instead of one huge, overloaded configuration.

Example use case ￼

- One profile for personal hacking (my own tools, models, repos).
- One profile per client / employer (their tools, providers, repos, security rules).
- For example, I currently maintain multiple configurations (including ‎`oh-my-opencode`‑based setups) and have to juggle them manually; profiles would let me encode these as first‑class switches inside OpenCode itself.

Possible implementation ￼

- Introduce a Profile abstraction that:
  - Points to a config root and optional overrides (models, tools, env).
  - Is persisted and selectable from the UI and command palette.
  - Reload active configuration when the profile changes, without needing manual file juggling.

    2. Via a command / keybinding.
- A clear indicator of the current profile so I don’t accidentally run the wrong config.

Why this is useful ￼

- Different contexts (personal, work, different clients) need very different configurations and constraints.

- Today, I have to:
    1.  Manually swap configuration folders / files.
    2.  Restart or reload things to pick up the new setup.
    3.  Remember which config is currently active, which is error‑prone.

- Profiles would:
    1.  Make context switching fast and safe.
    2.  Keep work and personal / client setups clearly separated.
    3.  Encourage focused, minimal configs instead of one huge, overloaded configuration.

Example use case ￼

- One profile for personal hacking (my own tools, models, repos).
- One profile per client / employer (their tools, providers, repos, security rules).
- For example, I currently maintain multiple configurations (including ‎`oh-my-opencode`‑based setups) and have to juggle them manually; profiles would let me encode these as first‑class switches inside OpenCode itself.

Possible implementation ￼

- Introduce a Profile abstraction that:
  - Points to a config root and optional overrides (models, tools, env).
  - Is persisted and selectable from the UI and command palette.
  - Reload active configuration when the profile changes, without needing manual file juggling.

items.title: Object does not respond to mouse events

raw.title: Object does not respond to mouse events
raw.body:
I have a JS script that swaps out an element's inner text with an alternative held in a data-* attribute:

<span data-swapinnertext="new text">old text</span>

I have been using this, and it works fine to a point. The point being that there's only one swap on the page:

function swapInnerText0() {
  if (document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]').length > 0) {
    var s, spans = document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]');
    for (s = 0; s < spans.length; s++) {
      var swapText = spans[s].dataset.swapinnertext, innerText = spans[s].innerText;
      spans[s].onmouseover = function() {
        this.innerText = swapText;
      }
      spans[s].onmouseout = function() {
        this.innerText = innerText;
      }
      spans[s].onclick = function() {
        this.innerText = swapText;
        this.onmouseover = null;
        this.onmouseout = null;
        this.removeAttribute('data-swapinnertext');
      }
    }
  }
}

However, if there's more that one, then the onmouseout event replaces the text with the value from the last member of span[s]. I realize why this is the case, so I sought to fix it.

This works, creating temporary data-* cache attributes to hold the text versions for each element:

function swapInnerText1() {
  if (document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]').length > 0) {
    var s, spans = document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]');
    for (s = 0; s < spans.length; s++) {
      spans[s].setAttribute('data-swapcache1', spans[s].dataset.swapinnertext);
      spans[s].setAttribute('data-swapcache2', spans[s].innerText);
      spans[s].onmouseover = function() {
        this.innerText = this.dataset.swapcache1;
      }
      spans[s].onmouseout = function() {
        this.innerText = this.dataset.swapcache2;
      }
      spans[s].onclick = function() {
        this.innerText = this.dataset.swapcache1;
        this.onmouseover = null;
        this.onmouseout = null;
        this.removeAttribute('data-swapinnertext');
        this.removeAttribute('data-swapcache1');
        this.removeAttribute('data-swapcache2');
      }
    }
  }
}

But it is inelegant. What I had tried to earlier do was create a 2D array of the elements and use that to ensure that the text versions for each element were separated from the others:

function swapInnerText2() {
  if (document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]').length > 0) {
    var sp, sw, spans = document.querySelectorAll('span[data-swapinnertext]'), swaps = Array();
    for (sp = 0; sp < spans.length; sp++) {
      var swapText = spans[sp].dataset.swapinnertext, innerText = spans[sp].innerText;
      swaps.push(Array(swapText, innerText));
    } 
    for (sw = 0; sw < swaps.length; sw++) {
      var newText = swaps[sw][0], oldText = swaps[sw][1];
      swaps[sw].onmouseover = function() {
        this.innerText = newText;
      }
      swaps[sw].onmouseout = function() {
        this.innerText = oldText;
      }
      swaps[sw].onclick = function() {
        this.innerText = newText;
        this.onmouseover = null;
        this.onmouseout = null;
        this.removeAttribute('data-swapinnertext');
      }
    }
  }
}

And this is where things go weird. None of the swaps[sw] objects respond to the mouse events. I placed alert() outside the anonymous functions, and they picked up that swaps[sw] were objects, the index and text values for each one, but within the functions nothing happened.

I've racked what little brain I have, and searched extensively, but simply cannot understand why the mouse events don't work in the third version—which I prefer over the second—but do in the other two.

The goal is to create a non-recursive type which will able to detect if the passed string contains only alphabet characters (TS version is 5.9.3)

const c: Special = '1'; // OK

type IsAlphabet<T extends string> = T extends `${string}${Special}${string}` ? never : T;

type Testing = IsAlphabet<"1">; // 1

I don't know why but Exclude<Lowercase<string> & Uppercase<string>, ''> doesn't exclude the empty string

Third attempt (step by step):

type Special = `${SpecialChar}${string}`;

const a: Special = ''; // Type 'string' is not assignable to type '`${SpecialChar}${string}`'

type IsAlphabet<T extends string> = T extends Special ? never : (

      T extends`${string}${Special}${string}` ? never : T

Attempted Fixes

There is a catch to all of this. If we run a simple node function outside of the application:

import { createReadStream } from "node:fs";
import { stat } from "node:fs/promises";

export async function putPresignedS3(url, filename) {
  const fileStat = await stat(filename);

  const res = await fetch(url, {
    method: "PUT",
    duplex: "half",
    headers: {
      "Content-Type": "application/octet-stream",
      "Content-Length": String(fileStat.size),
    },
    body: createReadStream(filename),
  });

  if (!res.ok) {
    const text = await res.text().catch(() => "");
    throw new Error(`Upload failed: HTTP ${res.status}\n${text}`);
  }

  console.log(res.status);
}

it will successfully hit with the signed URL that we have created. That puts us at a total loss for what is going wrong.

items.title: Why is callback reference not observed in useEffect

raw.title: Why is callback reference not observed in useEffect
raw.body:
How do I render a div in a component conditionally based on a component property and the get a reference to that div when it's available?

In this simplified example, the message displayed in the div varies depending on which button is pressed first. I understand why I see div.current is truthy when pressing the second button first. I don't understand why useEffect doesn't observe the change of the div loading upon the change of showHere.

const Message = ({ showHere }) => {
  const divRef = useRef(null);
  useEffect(() => {
    if (divRef.current) {
      divRef.current.innerHTML = "div.current is truthy";
    }
  }, [divRef, divRef.current]);

  return <>{showHere ? <div ref={divRef}>no message</div> : ""}</>;
};

export default function App() {
  const [showInsideApp, setShowInsideApp] = useState(false);
  const [showInsideComponent, setShowInsideComponent] = useState(false);
  const onButton1Clicked = () => {
    setShowInsideApp(true);
  };
  const onButton2Clicked = () => {
    setShowInsideComponent(true);
  };
  return (
    <div>
      {showInsideApp ? <Message showHere={showInsideComponent} /> : ""}
      <button onClick={onButton1Clicked}>Show in App</button>
      <button onClick={onButton2Clicked}>Show in Component</button>
    </div>
  );
}

The React documentation says:

The useRef Hook returns an object with a single property called current. Initially, myRef.current will be null. When React creates a DOM node for this , React will put a reference to this node into myRef.current. You can then access this DOM node from your event handlers and use the built-in browser APIs defined on it.

I've looked at this answer but it links to outdated documentation, and the current version is pretty different.

Based on this answer and this answer I can monitor on every render by entirely omitting useEffect's second parameter, but I don't want to do that. My real-world problem on which this is based on wanting to configure Coloris's parent element and attach a coloris:pick event to the window but only when the parent element is available.

items.title: input fields become uneditable until Developer Tools is opened

raw.title: input fields become uneditable until Developer Tools is opened
raw.body:
Context:

This is a production Electron desktop application. The issue occurs only on Windows and appears related to focus or hit-testing behaviour rather than application logic.

This is a production Electron desktop application. The issue occurs only on Windows and appears related to focus or hit-testing behavior rather than application logic.

Observed behavior:

Application starts and input fields are editable

Creating a new project still works

Creating the first item causes input fields (descriptions) to become uneditable

Clicking works but the cursor never appears

Typing does nothing and onFocus/onChange never fire

The macOS version works perfectly

Workaround:

Opening View → Toggle Developer Tools once immediately fixes the issue

Closing Developer Tools keeps inputs working

Creating another project breaks inputs again until Developer Tools is toggled

Technology stack:

Electron

React 18

Zustand

react-konva (canvas/PDF viewer overlay)

What we have tried:

Removing stopPropagation and preventDefault from inputs

Removing input onMouseDown handlers

Guarding parent click handlers

Disabling canvas pointer-events while typing

Forcing resize using ResizeObserver and requestAnimationFrame

None of these remove the need to toggle Developer Tools.

Question:
What does opening Developer Tools trigger in Electron or Chromium on Windows that resets focus or hit-testing, and how can this be replicated programmatically or prevented entirely?

This is a business application, so I cannot share the full repository, but I can provide a minimal non-proprietary reproduction if needed.
